A recipe is a component's variants in one place: a base style, named groups of
options, and the combinations that need a value of their own.

properties.html: import { recipe } from "@kirana-style/core" export const button = recipe({ base: { display: "inline-flex", alignItems: "center", borderRadius: "0.5rem", fontWeight: 500, }, variants: { tone: { solid: { backgroundColor: "black", color: "white" }, quiet: { backgroundColor: "transparent", color: "black" }, }, size: { sm: { paddingInline: "0.5rem", fontSize: "0.75rem" }, md: { paddingInline: "0.875rem", fontSize: "0.875rem" }, }, }, compoundVariants: [ { tone: "quiet", size: "sm", css: { paddingInline: "0.375rem" } }, ], defaultVariants: { tone: "solid", size: "md" }, }) <button sx={button({ tone: "quiet" })} />

children.value: Static calls compile to a constant

When the options are known at build time, the call disappears: the element gets a
class string, and no recipe table ships. When an option is a runtime value, the
recipe resolves through the small private runtime instead, and the compiler tells
you it did (

properties.source:
button({ tone: "quiet" }) // compiles to a constant
button({ tone: props.tone }) // resolved at runtime, reported as dynamic-variant
properties.html: button({ tone: "quiet" }) // compiles to a constant button({ tone: props.tone }) // resolved at runtime, reported as dynamic-variant

Both work. The diagnostic exists so you can see which components carry a runtime
cost.

A component with several parts gives them one recipe. Each variant lists the
slots it changes, and calling the recipe returns a handle per slot:

properties.html: export const field = recipe({ slots: ["root", "label", "input"], base: { root: { display: "grid", gap: "0.25rem" }, label: { fontSize: "0.875rem" }, input: { borderRadius: "0.375rem" }, }, variants: { invalid: { true: { label: { color: "crimson" }, input: { borderColor: "crimson" }, }, }, }, }) const parts = field({ invalid }) <div sx={parts.root}> <label sx={parts.label} /> <input sx={parts.input} /> </div>

An option that names a group or value the recipe does not define is an error

A style that names a slot the recipe does not declare is an error

Both catch the rename that used to leave a component silently unstyled.

Use a recipe when a component has variants a caller chooses by name. Use plain
handles when it does not: an object of

handles is simpler to read, and
merging already gives you composition:

properties.html: const styles = { root: css({ … }), open: css({ … }), } <div sx={[styles.root, isOpen && styles.open]} />
